Rashi on Yevamot 4b:10:1.hebrew: ותכלת עמרא - מדשש כיתנא, דכתי' (שמות ל״ט:כ״ח) מכנסי בד שש משזר, ובד היינו פשתים, כדמפרש בבא לו כ"ג במסכת יומא (דף עא:): בד — דבר העולה בד בבד. תכלת עמרא, וכן שאר צבעים האמורים בבגדי כהונה — ארגמן ותולעת שני — שאין בגדי כהונה אלא מצמר ופשתים, דכתיב בספר יחזקאל (מד) ביוה"כ: בגדי פשתים ילבשו ולא יעלה עליהם צמר; ש"מ שעבודות החיצונות יש בהם צמר עם פשתן, ולא מין אחר. ומדמפרש קרא שש באחד מן המינין, שמע מינה: שאר המינין צמר היו:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:10:1.english: And tekhelet is wool - [This is derived] from [the fact] that shesh is linen: As it is written (Exodus 39:28): “linen breeches of fine twined linen,” and bad means linen, as is explained in [the chapter] “Ba Lo Kohen Gadol” in Tractate Yoma (71b): “Bad — something that grows stalk by stalk.” [Therefore,] tekhelet is wool, and likewise the other colors mentioned regarding the priestly garments — argaman [purple wool] and tola'at shani [scarlet wool] — for the priestly garments are made only of wool and linen, as it is written in the Book of Ezekiel (44:17) regarding Yom Kippur: “They shall wear linen garments, and no wool shall come upon them.” Learn from this that [the garments for] the outer services contain wool with linen, and not any other material; and since Scripture specifies shesh for one of the materials, learn from this that the other materials were wool.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:11:1.hebrew: סד"א כדרבא - אי לא כתב רחמנא צמר ופשתים, הוה דרשי' הכנף מין כנף כרבא, למימר: דלבגד פשתים עשה פשתן, ולצמר עשה צמר וצבעי' תכלת, אבל כלאים — לא. קמ"ל דרשא דסמוכין, דאפילו כלאים. והכי הוי מסקנא דמילתא, אלא דקא מפרש ואזיל מילתי' דרבא:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:11:1.english: It could enter your mind to say in accordance with Rava - If the Merciful One had not written “wool and linen,” we would have expounded “the corner” [to mean fringes of the same] type as the corner, in accordance with Rava, to say that for a garment of linen, make [fringes of] linen, and for [a garment of] wool, make [fringes of] wool and dye it sky-blue [tekhelet], but diverse kinds [kilayim] — no. [Therefore,] the derivation of the juxtaposition teaches us that even diverse kinds [are permitted]. And that indeed is the conclusion of the matter, but [the Gemara] goes on to explain the statement of Rava [first].

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:11:2.hebrew: כתיב הכנף - עשה ציצית ממין הכנף, ואם טלית של משי — עשה ציצית של משי. וכתיב "צמר ופשתים", "גדילים תעשה לך", דמשמע: עשה ציצית מצמר ופשתים:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:11:2.english: It is written: "The corner" - Make fringes of the [same] material as the corner; and if [it is] a garment of silk, make fringes of silk. And it is written: "Wool and linen" [and] "You shall make yourself twisted cords," which implies: Make fringes of wool and linen.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:13:1.hebrew: והא תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל לית ליה דרבא - דדריש ״הכנף״ — מין כנף; דהא לתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, טלית של שאר מינין אינה חייבת בציצית, דהא ״בגד״ כתיב, ותנא דבי רבי ישמעאל קאמר: כל בגד — צמר ופשתים:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:13:1.english: But the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not hold in accordance with Rava - For [Rava] expounds 'the corner' [to mean fringes of the same] kind as the corner; for according to the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, a garment of other materials is not obligated in tzitzit, as 'garment' is written [in the verse], and the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael says: Every 'garment' [mentioned in the Torah is only of] wool and linen.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:14:1.hebrew: איצטריך - צמר ופשתים, אע"ג דלא דריש תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל מין כנף לשאר מינין:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:14:1.english: It is necessary - [To write] “wool and linen,” even though the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not expound “[fringes of the same] kind as the corner” for other kinds [of materials].

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:14:2.hebrew: סד"א - לגבי טלית של צמר ופשתים, דריש כי דיוקא דרבא, דדריש ציצית מין כנף:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:14:2.english: It could enter your mind to say - With regard to a garment of wool or linen, he [the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael] expounds in accordance with the inference of Rava, who expounds that the fringes [must be of the same] type as the corner.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:14:3.english: And this is what the Merciful One is saying, etc. - The derivation of the juxtaposition teaches us to permit diverse kinds [kilayim] in tzitzit.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:1:1.hebrew: לאפנויי - לאנוסתו של אביו, דיליף מסמוכים דלעיל:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:1:1.english: To free [it] - For [the case of] a woman raped by his father, which he derives from the juxtaposition above.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:2:1.english: “You shall not wear sha'atnez” — why do I need [it]? - Learn from this that [it is] to free [the verse] and to expound [the] juxtaposition.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:3:1.english: And even sellers of coverings - Who do not intend [to derive] the benefit of warmth.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:5:1.hebrew: צמר ופשתים למה לי - אי לאשמועינן דכלאים צמר ופשתים הוא דקאסר, לא צריך, דמכדי בכלאים כתיב בגד, ותנא דבי ר' ישמעאל כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:5:1.english: Why do I need “wool and linen”? - If [it is] to teach us that [the prohibition of] diverse kinds forbids [specifically] wool and linen — [this is] not needed, since regarding diverse kinds it is written “garment,” and the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught, etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:6:1.hebrew: באחד מהם - גבי נגעים: ״בבגד צמר או בבגד פשתים״ (ויקרא יג):
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:6:1.english: In one of them - Regarding [leprous] afflictions: “In a woolen garment or in a linen garment” (Leviticus 13).

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:7:1.hebrew: ואכתי איצטריך - למכתב צמר ופשתים הכא גבי לבישה, ואע"ג דכתיב בגד בהעלאה דמשמע צמר ופשתים, דס"ד כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:7:1.english: And it is still necessary - To write "wool and linen" here regarding wearing, even though it is written "garment" regarding placing [a garment on oneself], which implies wool and linen; for it could enter your mind [to say], etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:9:1.english: And the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael - For we derive according to him [the permissibility of] *kil'ayim* in *tzitzit* from [the fact] that "wool and linen" is superfluous, in order to juxtapose it to "You shall make yourself twisted cords."

Rashi on Yevamot 4b:9:2.hebrew: טעמא דכתב רחמנא כו' כל בגדים צמר ופשתים הם - והאי בגדיהם דציצית משמע בין של צמר בין של פשתים, ואמר רחמנא עביד, ותכלת נמי לפשתים:
Rashi on Yevamot 4b:9:2.english: The reason that the Merciful One wrote, etc., all garments are wool and linen - And this [word] 'their garments' regarding tzitzit means both of wool and of linen, and the Merciful One said to make [fringes], and [to place] *tekhelet* also on linen [garments].

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:1.hebrew: ותנא דבי ר' ישמעאל וכו' - וא"ת: בלא תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל נמי יוכל לדקדק, ד"בגדים" משמע כל בגדים, דלכולהו אמר רחמנא עביד להו תכלת, אלמא בבגדי פשתן נמי שרי תכלת! וכ"ת: דה"א דלאו אכולהו אמר רחמנא דליעבד תכלת — השתא נמי נימא דאצמר דוקא אמר רחמנא דליעבד תכלת, ולא אפשתים! וי"ל: דודאי אי לאו תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, ה"א דשאר מיני אמר רחמנא דליעבד תכלת, ולא אפשתים; אבל לתנא דבי רבי ישמעאל, דכל בגדים צמר ופשתים — משמע דאתרוייהו קאי; דאפי' נימא בעלמא ד"בגד" הוי או צמר או פשתים, הכא "בגדיהם" כתב, דמשמע תרי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:1.english: "And the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught," etc. - And if you should say: Even without [the teaching of] the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, one could also deduce that "garments" implies all garments, for regarding all of them the Merciful One said to make techelet for them, which proves that on linen garments too, techelet is permitted! And if you should say that we would have said that the Merciful One did not say to make techelet on all of them [and linen is excluded] — now too, let us say that the Merciful One said to make techelet specifically on wool, and not on linen! And one can say: Indeed, were it not for [the teaching of] the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, I would have said that the Merciful One said to make techelet on other materials, but not on linen; however, according to the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael, that all garments [in the Torah] are wool and linen, it implies that it refers to both of them. For even if we say that in general, [the singular term] "garment" means [either] wool or linen, here it wrote "their garments," which implies two [i.e., both types].

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:2.hebrew: ואמר רחמנא עביד להו תכלת - וא"ת: והיכי משמע מהכא דשרי כלאים בציצית? נימא דעביד להו תכלת בלא שוע, טווי ונוז! וי"ל, דחוטי ציצית בעינן שיהא שוע, טווי ונוז — דדריש בספרי: "פתיל תכלת" — טווי ושזור, וה"ה שוע דבעינן, ויליף התם לבן מתכלת. וסתם בגדים שלהן היו נמי שוע, טווי וגם נוזין — פירוש: שזורים, כמו שפי' ר"ת לקמן (יבמות ד' ה: ד"ה עד): "נוז" — שזורי; היינו שזורים בסוף הטלית, מקום הנחת ציצית, כדאמרינן בריש המוצא תפילין (עירובין צו:): "ודלמא אדעתא דשיפתא דגלימא עייפינהו". אבל קשיא: דאכתי נימא דאמר רחמנא לעביד להו תכלת בלא קשירה, דלא הוי כלאים, דתוכף תכיפה אחת אין חיבור! ובמנחות (דף לט.) דקדק דקשר עליון דאורייתא, מדשרי רחמנא כלאים בציצית. ושמעתי בשם ר"י קלנו', דע"כ אמר רחמנא ליעביד להו תכלת בענין דהוי כלאים; דאי דוקא בלא כלאים, א"כ לישתוק קרא מ"יחדו", ומדאמר רחמנא "עביד להו תכלת" ידעי דתוכף תכיפה אחת אינו חיבור. אלא ודאי בענין דהוי כלאים אמר רחמנא ליעביד תכלת, ולא שמעינן להו מהכא מידי אי תוכף תכיפה אחת חיבור אי לא — להכי איצטריך "יחדו":
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:2.english: "And the Merciful One says: Prepare sky-blue [threads] for them" - And if you say: And how is it implied from here that diverse kinds (kilayim) are permitted in tzitzit? Let us say that one makes sky-blue [threads] for them without [the fibers being] carded, spun, and twisted! And one can say: For with regard to tzitzit threads, we require that [each] be carded, spun, and twisted, as [the Sages] expound in the Sifrei: "A cord of sky-blue" — spun and twisted; and the same applies to carded, which we require; and there it derives [the requirement for the] white [threads] from [that of the] sky-blue [threads]. And their standard garments were also carded, spun, and also nozin — meaning twisted [threads] — as Rabbeinu Tam explained below (Yevamot 5b, s.v. Ad): "Noz" [means] twisted; that is, twisted at the edge of the cloak, the place where tzitzit are attached, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] HaMotzeh Tefillin (Eruvin 96b): "And perhaps they folded them with the border of the cloak in mind." However, it is [still] difficult: for still, let us say that the Merciful One said to make sky-blue [threads] for them without tying, so that it is not kilayim, as inserting a single stitch is not a connection! And in Menachot (39a), [the Gemara] inferred that the upper knot is biblical from [the fact] that the Merciful One permitted kilayim in tzitzit. And I heard in the name of Rabbi Y. Kalonymus that perforce the Merciful One said to make sky-blue [threads] for them in a manner that constitutes kilayim; for if [the Torah meant] specifically without kilayim, if so, let the verse be silent regarding [the word] "together," and from [the fact] that the Merciful One said: "Prepare sky-blue [threads] for them," we would know that inserting a single stitch is not a connection! Rather, certainly the Merciful One said to make sky-blue [threads] in a manner that constitutes kilayim, and [consequently] we cannot derive anything from here as to whether inserting a single stitch is a connection or not; for that [reason], "together" was necessary.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:3.hebrew: ותכלת עמרא הוא - לא היה צריך לכך, דבין הוא כיתנא ובין הוא עמרא יכול לדקדק דכלאים בציצית שרי; דאמר רחמנא לבגדיהם, דהוו צמר ופשתים, ליעביד תכלת, שהוא או כיתנא או עמרא — שאין בבגדי כהונה אלא צמר ופשתים, מדכתב בהו "בגדיהם". אלא האמת אומר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:3.english: "And tekhelet is wool" - [The Tanna] did not need [to state] this, for whether it is linen or whether it is wool, he could deduce that diverse kinds [kilayim] are permitted in ritual fringes [tzitzit]; for the Merciful One said that for "their garments" — which are wool and linen — one should make tekhelet, which is either linen or wool — as there is nothing in the priestly garments other than wool and linen, since [Scripture] wrote regarding them "their garments." Rather, he is stating the truth.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:4.hebrew: מדשש כיתנא תכלת עמרא - וליכא למימר דתכלת נמי כיתנא, אלא צבוע הוא תכלת, וארגמן ותולעת שני עמרא — דסברא הוא דכל הצבועים מין אחד הוא, מדלא חילק בהן אלא בצבע:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:10:4.english: "From [the fact] that shesh is linen, tekhelet is wool" - And one cannot say that tekhelet is also linen, only it is dyed [with] tekhelet, while argaman [purple] and tola'at shani [scarlet] are wool — for it stands to reason that all the dyed [materials] are of one kind, since [Scripture] did not distinguish among them except by color.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:11:1.hebrew: סלקא דעתך אמינא כדרבא - לאו דוקא: דרבא איירי בתר דכתיב צמר ופשתים, והשתא איירי אי לא כתב צמר ופשתים; אלא כלומר, כדיוקא דרבא. וה"ק קרא: "ועשו להם ציצית על כנפי בגדיהם" — דלבגדיהם, שהם צמר ופשתים, עביד ציצית; אבל תכלת דבתר הכי, לא קאי אבגדים, אלא אהכנף — מין כנף. והמקשה דפריך: "והא תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל לית ליה דרבא", וסבור דכרבא ממש קאמר — היה יכול להקשות: והא רבא לבתר דכתיב צמר ופשתים קאמר:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:11:1.english: “It could enter your mind to say in accordance with Rava” - [This] is not exact, for Rava is speaking after “wool and linen” is written, whereas here [the Gemara] is dealing with [the scenario where the Torah] had not written “wool and linen”; rather, [the Gemara] means: in accordance with Rava’s deduction. And this is what the verse means: “That they make themselves fringes on the corners of their garments” — that for their garments, which are [specifically] wool and linen, one makes fringes; but the sky-blue [thread (tekhelet)] that is [mentioned] after this does not refer to “garments,” but rather to “the corner” — [threads of] the same type as the corner. And the questioner who objects: “But the tanna from the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not maintain in accordance with Rava,” and who assumed that [the Gemara] meant literally like Rava — could have objected: But behold, Rava speaks after “wool and linen” is written!

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:13:1.hebrew: והא תנא דבי ר' ישמעאל לית ליה דרבא - דליכא למימר דמהכנף מרבה שאר בגדים, כדאשכחן בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת כז. ושם) דמרבה שאר בגדים גבי שרצים מאו בגד — דהכנף לאו ריבויא הוא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:13:1.english: "But the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not hold like Rava" - For one cannot say that from "hakanaf" [the corner] he includes other garments, as we find in the chapter [entitled] "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 27a and ibid.) that he includes other garments with regard to [the impurity of] creeping animals from "or a garment" — for "hakanaf" is not an inclusion.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:14:1.hebrew: ואפילו צמר לפשתים ופשתים לצמר - משמע הכא דתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל לית ליה דרבא. וקשה, דבפ' במה מדליקין (כ"ז. שם) קאמר הש"ס: "הדר ביה רבא מההיא", וסבר ד"אף כל" לאתויי שרצים, וסבר שפיר כתנא דבי ר' ישמעאל. וצ"ל, דסוגיא דהכא כר"נ בר יצחק דהתם, דקאי "אף כל" לאיתויי ציצית — א"כ, הוי דלא כרבא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:14:1.english: "And even wool for linen and linen for wool" - It is implied here that the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael does not hold in accordance with [the view of] Rava. And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "Bameh Madlikin" (Shabbat 27a), the Gemara says: "Rava retracted from that [statement]," and held that "so too all" comes to include creeping animals [sheratzim], and he indeed agrees with the Tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael. And it must be said that the sugya here is in accordance with [the view of] Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak there, [who maintains] that "so too all" applies to include ritual fringes [tzitzit]; if so, it is [indeed] not in accordance with Rava.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:14:2.hebrew: דאפילו צמר לפשתן ופשתן לצמר כו' - נראה, דאפילו שני חוטין לבן של צמר שרי בפשתים, כדאמר במנחות, אף על גב דאפשר במינו — כדקאמר התם: מגו דתכלת פטרה, לבן נמי פוטר. ולבן של פשתים נמי פוטר הצמר על מגו דמגו: דלבן של צמר פוטר בפשתים, לבן של פשתים נמי פוטר בצמר. ודוקא במקום תכלת, אבל במקום שאין תכלת — אסור, כיון דלא כשר במינו; דהא במנחות (דף מ.) אסר סדין בציצית משום קלא אילן, ופריך: ולא יהא אלא לבן, ומשני: משום דאפשר במינן, כדר"ל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:14:2.english: "That even wool for linen and linen for wool, etc." - It appears that even two white strings of wool are permitted on [a garment of] linen, as [the Gemara] says in Menachot [39b–40a], even though it is possible [to use strings] of its own kind — as it says there: Since tekhelet exempts [the linen garment from the prohibition of kilayim], the white [wool strings] also exempt [it]. And white [strings] of linen also exempt [a garment of] wool based on a miggo of a miggo: Since white [strings] of wool exempt [a garment of] linen, white [strings] of linen also exempt [a garment of] wool. And [this applies] specifically in a situation where there is tekhelet; but where there is no tekhelet, it is forbidden, since it is not valid [unless made] of its own kind. For in Menachot (40a), [the Gemara] prohibited [affixing fringes to] a linen sheet due to [the concern of fraudulent] indigo [kala ilan], and objects: "And let it be merely [treated as] white [strings]?" And it answers: Because it is possible [to fulfill the mitzvah with strings] of their own kind, in accordance with [the principle of] Reish Lakish.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:2:1.hebrew: מכדי כתיב ובגד כלאים וגו' - ההוא קרא דגדילים לא מצית לאייתורי ולמימר: "מכדי כתיב פרשת ציצית, למאי הילכתא כתביה?" — דכולה איצטריך, כדדרשינן לקמן (יבמות דף ה:): "גדילים" — ארבעה; ודרשינן נמי: "על ד' כנפות" — ולא על ג' וה'; "כסותך" — ולא של אחרים; "אשר תכסה בה" — פרט לכסות סומא, ולמעט שאין מכסה רובו:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:2:1.english: "Now, since it is written: 'Neither shall there come upon you a garment of diverse kinds,' etc." - You could not consider that verse of gedilim [twisted fringes] superfluous and say: "Now, since the portion of tzitzit is [already] written, for what halakha did [the Torah] write it?" — for all of it is necessary, as we derive below (5b): "Gedilim" [teaches that there must be] four [strings]; and we also derive: "Upon the four corners" — and not upon three or five [corners]; "Your garment" — and not [the garment] of others; "Wherewith you cover yourself" — excluding the garment of a blind person, and to exclude [a garment] that does not cover the majority of [one's body].

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:7:1.hebrew: אבל לבישה כל תרי מיני אסר רחמנא - וא"ת: אפילו חד מינא ה"א דאסור, ובלבד שיהא שוע, טווי ונוז? וי"ל: דשעטנז משמע נמי תערובות:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:7:1.english: "However, [with regard to] wearing, the Merciful One prohibited any two types" - And if you say: Even a single type one would have said is prohibited, provided that it is combed, spun, and woven? And one can say: "Shaatnez" also implies a mixture.

Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:8:1.hebrew: אם כן לשתוק קרא מיניה ותיתי שעטנז שעטנז מהעלא' - וא"ת: בפ' במה מדליקין (שבת כז: ושם) קאמר רב פפא, אף כל צמר ופשתים דקאמר רבי ישמעאל לאיתויי כלאים; וקאמר התם דהא דרב פפא בדותא היא, דכלאים צמר ופשתים בהדיא כתב בהו. ומאי קושיא? והא איצטריך אף כל לאפנויי צמר ופשתים, כדקאמר הכא! וי"ל: דבמסקנא, דנפקא לן הפנאה לרבנן משעטנז — לר' ישמעאל נמי תיפוק מהתם, ותו לא איצטריך אף כל לאפנויי צמר ופשתים דכלאים:
Tosafot on Yevamot 4b:8:1.english: “If so, let the verse be silent from it, and let [it] be derived [via] ‘sha’atnez’ [and] ‘sha’atnez’ from placing [upon oneself]” - And if you say: In chapter Bameh Madlikin (Shabbat 27b and there), Rav Pappa says [that the rule] “so too, all [garments are of] wool and linen” which Rabbi Yishmael stated [comes] to include diverse kinds [kilayim]; and [the Gemara] says there that this [statement] of Rav Pappa is an error, since regarding diverse kinds, “wool and linen” is explicitly written concerning them. And what is the difficulty? But isn’t “so too, all” needed to free up “wool and linen,” as [the Gemara] says here? And it can be answered that in the conclusion [of the Gemara], where the freeing [of the term] is derived according to the Rabbis from “sha’atnez,” for Rabbi Yishmael as well let it be derived from there, and furthermore, “so too, all” was no longer needed to free up “wool and linen” of diverse kinds.
